stories.title: Biden among tributes to Mayo after All-Ireland win
stories.summary: Former US President Joe Biden has led tributes to the Mayo team after their All-Ireland win yesterday. The Mayo football team is regarded as one of the best in the country but has repeatedly fallen short of winning the top prize of the Sam Maguire Cup in the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship. The repeated final losses have seen the hopeful mantra of "Mayo for Sam" gain prominence, referring to the Sam Maguire Cup. Mayo had not won the cup in 75 years despite reaching the final 11 times since 1989.

stories.title: France braces for fresh heatwave as fires rage on
stories.summary: Firefighters were battling massive blazes tearing through forests across France and Spain today, as authorities warned of a fresh heatwave set to engulf the scorched French wine-growing region around the major city of Bordeaux. More than 325,000 people have fled their homes, mostly in the Gironde department, home to Bordeaux, as some of the worst forest fires in either country's history rage across southwest France and central Spain near Madrid. France's fire has caused an unprecedented 'pyrocumulonimbus' - a giant fire cloud that creates its own winds and packs lightning that causes more blazes, said the National Firefighters Federation of France (FNSPF). "It's a David-versus-Goliath scenario ... at some point, we'll find a weak spot and strike there," said FNSPF spokesman Eric Brocardi.

stories.title: Three dead after shooting at Seattle food festival
stories.summary: Three people have been killed and at least four others wounded, including a toddler, after an apparent gunfight near the Space Needle landmark in Seattle last night, according to police. Seattle Police said one suspect had been arrested and they were searching for another following the incident at the Bite of Seattle food festival in a popular tourist district of the northwestern US city. Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis said shots were heard around 6pm (2am Irish time) and "there were two people who we believe were shooting at each other." Two weapons were recovered. Police said on X earlier Sunday there were "multiple shooting victims" after shots were fired at the Seattle Center.

stories.title: Phoenix Park reopens historic Magazine Fort to the public
stories.summary: The Office of Public Works will officially reopen the Magazine Fort in Phoenix Park today. The historic site, designed by military engineer John Corneille, was built between 1734 and 1736 as a military storage facility. Ammunition and gunpowder, which had previously been stored in Dublin Castle, were moved to the fort after it was deemed a safer location outside the city. The fort later played a significant role in the Easter Rising, when it was raided on Easter Monday, 24 April 1916.

stories.title: Off-duty garda killed in single-vehicle crash in Co Clare
stories.summary: An off-duty garda was killed in a single-vehicle car crash in Co Clare yesterday evening. The collision happened shortly after 5.30pm yesterday on the R466 outside the village of Broadford. Gardaí and emergency services attended the scene, where the passenger of the car, was pronounced dead. The garda, a man in his 50s, was based at a station in Limerick city.

stories.title: Brazil recalls ambassador to Argentina over Milei speech
stories.summary: Brazil has recalled its ambassador to Argentina for consultations following "insults" levelled by President Javier Milei against his Brazilian counterpart Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. The comments were made by Mr Milei at a Sao Paulo political event, the foreign ministry said. The libertarian leader of Argentina referred to Brazil's leftist incumbent president as a "convict" and a "thief", without naming him explicitly, during an event on Saturday formally nominating right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro to run in upcoming elections. Mr Milei also referred to - without naming him directly - Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes as "bald trash."

stories.title: Ukraine air attacks kill two, wound 17 in Russia's south
stories.summary: Ukrainian air attacks have killed two people and wounded 17 others in strikes on the southern Russian cities of Rostov-on-Don and Belgorod, regional authorities have said. In Ukraine, Russian strikes killed one person and wounded seven others, local authorities said. In Rostov-on-Don, a major export hub near the Sea of Azov, a couple from the same family was killed and another five people were wounded, including two of whom were in critical condition, regional governor Yuri Slyusar said in a Telegram post. Falling drone debris caused fires at a number of locations, including warehouses, and windows were blown out in a residential apartment building, he added.

stories.title: 'Consumed by hate' - Infantino hits back at critics
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has hit back at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives while defending the tournament as a success that celebrated unity, safety and inclusion. In an open letter published on Monday, Infantino, 56, said detractors had overlooked the joy and togetherness experienced by millions of fans around the world who witnessed the tournament, won by Spain and staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico. "You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all," he said. "To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best ‌show in the world.
